questions.question_text: Which normal form deals with removing transitive dependencies from a relation?

options.explanation: 2NF removes partial dependencies on composite candidate keys.
3NF requires a relation to be in 2NF and have no transitive functional dependencies X -> Y where neither X is a super key nor Y is a prime attribute.
BCNF is a stricter version of 3NF where for every functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a super key.

options.text: More than one of the above / None of the above

questions.overall_explanation: A relation is in Third Normal Form (3NF) if it is in 2NF and no non-prime attribute is transitively dependent on the primary key. Removing transitive dependency prevents update, insertion, and deletion anomalies.
questions.concept_summary: 3NF removes transitive dependencies (X -> Y and Y -> Z => X -> Z).
questions.key_takeaway: Remember: 1NF = Atomic values, 2NF = No partial dependency, 3NF = No transitive dependency, BCNF = Every determinant is a super key.

questions.question_text: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for end-to-end communication, error recovery, and flow control?

options.explanation: Network layer handles routing and packet delivery across networks.
Transport Layer (Layer 4) provides transparent transfer of data between end systems and is responsible for end-to-end flow control and error control.
Data Link Layer provides node-to-node (hop-to-hop) framing and error control.
Session Layer manages sessions between applications.
Transport layer is the correct answer.

questions.overall_explanation: The Transport Layer (OSI Layer 4) uses protocols like TCP and UDP to manage process-to-process data transmission, providing segmentation, flow control (windowing), and error control (checksums and retransmissions).
questions.key_takeaway: Hop-to-hop = Data Link Layer, Host-to-Host = Network Layer, Process-to-Process = Transport Layer.

questions.question_text: Which CPU scheduling algorithm gives the minimum average waiting time for a given set of processes?

options.explanation: FCFS can cause the convoy effect, increasing average waiting time.
RR is designed for time-sharing systems, not optimal waiting time.
SJF scheduling algorithm is provably optimal for minimizing average waiting time for a given set of processes.
Priority scheduling can lead to starvation and does not guarantee minimum average wait time.

questions.overall_explanation: Shortest Job First (SJF) schedules the process with the shortest CPU burst time first. Moving a short process before a long process decreases the waiting time of the short process more than it increases the waiting time of the long process, giving the lowest overall average waiting time.
questions.concept_summary: SJF is provably optimal for minimum average waiting time.
questions.key_takeaway: SJF yields minimum average wait time, but predicting future CPU burst lengths requires estimation techniques like exponential averaging.
